arguments.hashlong_64b_withSecret_data: rdi; pointer to the input bytes. Read on every path: the block/remaining stripes read input[0..1024*nbBlocks+64*rem), the last stripe reads input+len-64..len-1; never written
arguments.hashlong_64b_withSecret_length: rsi; input length in bytes (size_t), > 240. Dispatched on at 0x61db9e2 (cmp $0x80, 17..128), 0x61db9f2 (cmp $0xf0, 129..240) and 0x61dba48 (nbBlocks = (len-1) / blockBytes); multiplied by PRIME64_1 at 0x61dbe5b in the merge
arguments.hashlong_64b_withSecret_secret: rdx (kept in r9); pointer to the caller-supplied secret bytes. Read on every path: stripe windows secret[s*8..s*8+64), scramble window secret+secretLimit..+64, last-stripe window secret+secretLimit-7..+64, merge words secret+11..67; never written
arguments.hashlong_64b_withSecret_secretSize: rcx (kept in rbp); secret length in bytes, >= 136. secretLimit = secretSize - 64 at 0x61db9ff (lea -0x40(%rcx),%rcx); determines nbStripesPerBlock = secretLimit >> 3 and the block size; the last-stripe windows use secretSize - 71/-55/-39/-23

census.direct_calls_note: Whole-.text E8 scan found no call site to 0x61db940 and a whole-.text rip-relative lea scan found no reference to it. The binary's symbol table is stripped, so no exported-symbol entry can be cited either. The entry point is the withSecret one-shot itself; its len > 240 branch is the inline path modelled here, and its 129..240 branch tail-jumps to the len_129to240_64b helper at 0x61d7dc0 (PR #5606).
census.sibling_callers: The default one-shot ROCKSDB_XXH3_64bits (0x61db650) and withSeed (0x61dc0c0) dispatch their len > 240 branches to the hashLong helpers at 0x61d8510/0x61d9090 (PR #5601), which run against the fixed 192-byte kSecret; withSecret cannot use them because it runs against a caller-supplied secret. The 128-bit hashLong pair at 0x61d8a60/0x61d9bc0 (PR #5598) is the same body with the high64 merge kept

model.acc_init: Eight accumulators initialised to XXH3_INIT_ACC = {PRIME32_3, PRIME64_1, PRIME64_2, PRIME64_3, PRIME64_4, PRIME32_2, PRIME64_5, PRIME32_1} from the .rodata constants at 0x455960/0x455950/0x453a30/0x4525e0, the same addresses the default helper loads. acc[5] is 0x85EBCA77 (PRIME32_2)
model.blocks: nbBlocks = (len-1) / blockBytes full blocks, where blockBytes = ((secretSize-64) >> 3) << 6 (1024 bytes for a 192-byte secret, 576 for 136, 1536 for 256). Each stripe is one accumulate_512 over 64 input bytes against a 64-byte secret window sliding 8 bytes per stripe (secret + s*8, restarting at the caller secret each block). After each block, scrambleAcc with the secret + secretLimit window (acc[i] = (acc[i] ^ (acc[i] >> 47) ^ secret[i]) * 0x9E3779B1; the multiplier is the .rodata constant at 0x4562c0)
model.last_stripe: Always runs: accumulate_512 over input[len-64..len) against secret + secretLimit - 7 (windows at secret + secretSize - 71/-55/-39/-23)
model.merge: Result = mergeAcc(acc, secret + 11, len * PRIME64_1). mergeAcc folds four 128-bit products (acc[2i] ^ secret[16i]) * (acc[2i+1] ^ secret[16i+8]) low ^ high, then XXH3_avalanche. The eight merge-window words are loaded from the caller secret at secret+11, 19, 27, 35, 43, 51, 59, 67 (xor disp(%r9)), not folded as immediates as in the default helper. This is the same merge as the low64 half of the 128-bit pair (PR #5598); the high64 merge is dropped
model.remaining_stripes: ((len-1) % blockBytes) >> 6 stripes from the block boundary, secret restarting at secret + 0
model.secret_limit: secretLimit = secretSize - 64 (lea -0x40(%rcx),%rcx at 0x61db9ff). It sets the stripes per block and the scramble/last-stripe windows; the raw secretSize is kept in rbp for the last-stripe addressing

semantics.scope: Lengths > 240 only, the inline path at 0x61db9ff inside the withSecret entry point, secretSize >= 136. Lengths 0..128 are reconstructed in PR #5449 (short branches and the 17..128 sweep) and 129..240 go through the len_129to240_64b helper at 0x61d7dc0 (PR #5606); with this packet the withSecret entry point -- and therefore all three 64-bit one-shots -- is reconstructed for every length
semantics.seed_term: There is no seed argument on this entry point: the caller secret is used as-is. The merge start uses len * PRIME64_1 with no seed term

side_effects: The inline path writes no memory, calls nothing except the stack-canary failure stub, and reads only [data, data+len) and the secret windows listed in the model. It restores all callee-saved registers and returns through the shared avalanche epilogue at 0x61db9a3

tests.cases: 2,400 deterministic cases (lengths 241..2048; secrets: the published kSecret, 11 random 192-byte secrets, and random secrets of sizes 136/144/160/176/200/208/224/256). Transliteration vs independent loop-form reference: 0 mismatches. See result.json
tests.native_execution_check: No native-execution check was repeated for this path. The same body shape was checked by native execution of the extracted bytes for the 128-bit pair (PR #5598: 120 cases, 0 mismatches); the oracle check below exercises this exact inline path through the withSecret entry-point dispatch, and the committed cross-check is the Python reference
tests.oracle_check: The transliteration agrees with the system libxxhash 0.8.2 oracle at the withSecret entry point (XXH3_64bits_withSecret, lengths 241..5000, secret sizes 136..256): 0/600 mismatches in a random sweep; all 7 check values confirmed; the oracle is not an input to the generator
tests.published_anchors: No published test vector exists for this path in isolation; the check values in check-values.tsv are computed values confirmed against the system oracle at the entry point. The three kSecret check values equal PR #5601's default-helper values, as the inline path with the default secret is the same algorithm
tests.unit_tests: tests/test_xxh3_hashlong_64b_withsecret115.py, 12 tests (check values, out-of-scope rejection, transliteration-vs-reference agreement over all boundary lengths and secret sizes, secret sensitivity, kSecret equivalence with the default helper, secret-window sensitivity, secret-size geometry, binary grounding including dispatch sites and the no-caller scan, result regeneration)

unknowns: Whether any caller outside the binary reaches the withSecret entry point is not established beyond the whole-.text E8/lea scan (no call site, no lea reference) and the stripped symbol table
No source-level rationale is claimed for the merge window starting at secret+11, or for secretLimit being secretSize - 64; both are recorded as observed in the disassembly
Behaviour for secretSize < 136 is out of scope: the public contract requires >= 136 and the binary does not check, so the windows would run past a shorter supplied secret

window.extraction: .text bodies at file offset VA-0x1000 (the ELF section headers claim VA-0x10000, which does not match the hash-verified bytes); .rodata tables at file offset VA (0x97ec80, 0x4525e0-0x4562c0). Both mappings are verified by hash/byte comparison, not by the headers
window.objdump: Whole-function excerpt in xxh3_64bits_withsecret115.objdump.txt, GNU objdump 2.42 over the hash-verified parent-body slice (objdump -D -b binary -m i386:x86-64 --adjust-vma=0x61db940). The '<.data>:' label is binary-mode section naming, not a symbol; the inline range bytes are in xxh3_hashlong_64b_withsecret115.hex
